question: What is the primary physical characteristic of a stockinette used in orthopedics?
explanation: A stockinette is manufactured as a continuous knitted tube without seams to prevent localized skin irritation under casts. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is cotton commonly used as the material for orthopedic stockinettes?

options.A: It acts as a strong primary weight-bearing layer
options.B: It chemically hardens when exposed to water
options.C: It provides permanent waterproofing for the limb
options.D: It allows skin breathability and reduces moisture

explanation: Cotton fibers absorb minimal moisture and allow air circulation, which helps maintain skin integrity under a cast. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h1)

question: The main purpose of a stockinette under a cast is to...

options.A: speed up the drying time of plaster
options.D: protect the skin from abrasive materials

explanation: The fabric creates a smooth barrier that shields the epidermis from direct contact with rough casting tape. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient complains of a scratching sensation inside a newly applied forearm cast. What role did a poorly applied stockinette likely play?

options.A: Excessive padding causing a compartment syndrome
options.B: Inadequate venous return from tight wrapping
options.C: Chemical burns from synthetic resin drying
options.D: Failure to cover rough edges of the plaster

explanation: If the stockinette does not extend far enough past the cast edges, rough plaster or fiberglass can directly chafe the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which material choice is best suited for a modern waterproof cast system?
explanation: Synthetic stockinettes paired with specialized padding allow water to drain freely away from the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h3)

question: A key advantage of standard cotton stockinette over synthetic alternatives is its...

options.A: high resistance to stretching out of shape
options.D: ability to repel all body fluids entirely

explanation: Cotton offers high patient comfort and naturally absorbs normal skin perspiration. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why must a nurse ensure a stockinette is free of wrinkles before casting?

options.A: Wrinkles prevent the plaster from hardening properly in time
options.B: Wrinkles create high-pressure areas that can cause skin breakdown
options.C: Wrinkles trap excessive heat and cause immediate chemical burns
options.D: Wrinkles make the finished cast too heavy for the patient

explanation: Any crease or fold trapped under a rigid cast exerts uneven pressure against the skin, risking ischemia and ulceration. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: How far beyond the intended cast boundaries should the stockinette ideally extend?

options.B: Exactly at the cast edge line
options.C: Only at the upper proximal end

explanation: Extending the fabric past the cast edges allows the nurse to fold it back, creating a smooth, padded border. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is a major risk if a stockinette is applied with excessive tension?

options.A: Rapid dissolution of the cast material
options.B: Permanent discoloration of the outer cast
options.D: Immediate infection of deep muscle tissue

explanation: A stockinette that is too narrow or pulled too tightly can restrict blood flow like a tourniquet. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: What should a nurse check first when evaluating a limb encased in a stockinette and plaster cast?

options.B: The exact brand of the casting tape
options.C: The length of the excess folded fabric
options.D: The weight of the dried plaster shell

explanation: Neurovascular checks prioritize blood flow and nerve function distal to the immobilized area. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: What warning should nurses give patients regarding itching under a stockinette and cast?

options.A: Use a wooden stick for safe scratching relief
options.B: Pour warm water down the tube to cool the skin
options.C: Never insert objects inside the cast to scratch
options.D: Apply greasy oil directly onto the fabric edge

explanation: Inserting foreign items can break fragile skin hidden beneath the layers, leading to severe localized infection. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which sign reported by a patient requires immediate clinical investigation of the cast area?

options.A: A foul odor or hot spot on the cast
options.B: Itching relieved by cool air from a fan
options.C: Dry skin flakes near the open cast edge
options.D: Normal mild muscle weakness from rest

explanation: Foul odors and localized warmth often indicate underlying skin breakdown, pressure necrosis, or infection. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)
